objective: Give a deactivated account (User.deleted_at set) a state the client can see and a way back: every route resolves its caller through one of three dependency paths (public read, active account, own account), a deactivated caller is refused on the active path with a recognisable 403, and POST /users/me/recover reactivates the caller's own account.
acceptance_criteria: get_current_user (the active-account path) answers 403 with detail exactly "account_deactivated" when the verified token's sub belongs to a User whose deleted_at is set, and 404 "User profile not found" (unchanged) when no User row has that sub.

A new dependency app.users.dependencies.get_own_account (the own-account path) returns the caller's own User row whether or not deleted_at is set, answers 404 when no row has the token's sub, and answers 401 exactly as get_current_identity does for a missing, malformed or rejected token.
get_optional_current_user (the public-read path) returns None for a deactivated caller's valid token, the same as for no Authorization header, and still answers 401 for a present but invalid token.

GET /users/me answers 403 {"detail": "account_deactivated"} for a deactivated caller, 200 MeOut for an active one and 404 for a token with no User row; the 403 is declared in the route's OpenAPI responses.

POST /users/me/recover clears deleted_at on the caller's own User row and answers 200 MeOut; called by an active account it changes nothing and answers 200 MeOut; called with a token whose sub has no User row it answers 404. It reads no user id from the path, query or body, so no caller can recover another account.
Recovery writes User.deleted_at and nothing else: every posts, follows, likes and notifications row is identical before and after a recover.
DELETE /users/me sets deleted_at on an active caller and answers 204; a second DELETE /users/me by the now-deactivated caller answers 204 and leaves the first deleted_at value unchanged.

One bearer token, issued before deactivation and unchanged throughout (the same FakeTokenVerifier token string), succeeds on POST /posts and POST /users/{id}/follow; after DELETE /users/me it gets 403 "account_deactivated" on both, and 200 guest behaviour on GET /feed and GET /users/{another id}; after POST /users/me/recover it succeeds on both writes again.
While an account is deactivated its GET /users/{id} answers 404 and its posts are absent from GET /feed and GET /search/posts; after recovery the profile answers 200 and the same posts appear again.
POST /users with a token whose sub already has a deactivated User row answers 409 and creates no second row.

A test walks every APIRoute registered on app.main's app and fails for any route with a method other than GET or HEAD whose dependency tree does not contain get_current_user, except an allowlist of exactly POST /users (identity only: no account exists yet), POST /users/me/recover and DELETE /users/me (own-account path). The same test fails if an allowlisted route no longer exists, and if an allowlisted route's tree contains neither get_current_identity nor get_own_account.

Every existing write route keeps its current behaviour for an active caller: the whole existing backend suite passes, with only assertions about a deactivated caller's status code changed from 404 to 403.

backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts are regenerated (python scripts/export_openapi.py, then npm run gen:api-types) and the frontend's typecheck and test suite pass with no other frontend change.
